text: {"standards":[{"code":"RL.6.9","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the 'The Oracle in the Novel and the Oracle in the Article' activity, students compare the article's central idea and details with the novel's Oracle scene and state a similarity and a difference in how each text presents the same figure."},{"code":"L.6.4","verdict":"taught","reason":"In 'Break the Word Apart' and 'Context Clues and the Unit Vocabulary Organizer,' students use prefixes, roots and context clues to determine the meanings of unknown words such as retreated, summoned, shredded and shrieked."},{"code":"L.6.5.a","verdict":"taught","reason":"In 'Interpreting the Oracle's Imagery,' students find figurative phrases such as the mist's tendrils, explain their literal meaning, and interpret what they suggest in context."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"uses","reason":"The lesson names Britannica Kids' 'Delphi – Kids' article in the comparison activity and pairs it with Chapter 9 (pp. 139–148), matching the Outline's texts and pages, though it allows 'or similar' articles."}}
